text:
Sam: FYI customer AcmeX just escalated — invoice for Feb shows ~1.18M tokens, but their dashboard 'served tokens' for the same window shows ~880k. They think we double-counted some warmups/prefetches. Requesting quick triage. request_id=req_0x7c8f1a
Ivy: Can you paste a couple example request IDs + timestamps? also want the invoice id so billing can correlate.
Sam: invoice INV-2026-02-73, example request ids: req_0x7c8f1a (2026-02-15T21:14:02Z), req_0x7c8fa0 (2026-02-15T21:14:14Z). Customer says many of these were fast chat responses but billed tokens are higher than visible.
Alyssa: quick note from runtime: we have an account-level prefetch policy for AcmeX (continuous batching + prefix prefetch enabled). That policy warms KV cache by issuing hidden model calls to generate prefixes for similar contexts. Those hidden warmup calls currently get recorded by the metering pipeline as regular model calls (they traverse same call path), but our dashboard served-token aggregation filters them out because they are tagged internal in the UI feed. In short: meter counts include warmup calls; dashboard served excludes them -> invoice > dashboard.
Kunal: to confirm: warmup calls actually consume model tokens (and thus cost us), right? so invoices reflecting raw metered tokens would include them.
Alyssa: correct. Warmup calls produce tokens from the model (they're real requests), so metering increments. The dashboard 'served tokens' view intentionally shows end-user-facing tokens and strips internal warmups for readability; we didn't align the invoice aggregation with that filter.
Sam: customer unhappy — requests a breakdown and potential credit if warmups explain the delta.
Ivy: quick repro snippet I pulled from logs (trimmed):
```
2026-02-15T21:14:01Z req=req_0x7c8f1a type=client_call tokens_in=12 tokens_out=48 route=/chat model=rwkv-13b
2026-02-15T21:14:02Z req=req_prefetch_0x7c8f1a type=prefetch tokens_in=60 tokens_out=120 route=/internal/prefetch model=rwkv-13b
2026-02-15T21:14:02Z req=req_0x7c8f1a type=client_call tokens_in=12 tokens_out=48 served=true
```
Sam: so you can see the `req_prefetch_` entry — counted by metering pipeline but filtered from served.
Alyssa: next steps from eng side: (1) short-term workaround: disable prefix prefetch for this account or set prefetch sampling lower; (2) medium-term: flag internal prefetch calls with metering_exclude=true so invoices & metering report align with served view; (3) permanent: add billing-side report that exposes "raw metered tokens" vs "user-facing served tokens". I've opened ENG-12345 to track.
Kunal: how do we disable for a single account? can support do it now?
Alyssa: yes, we can toggle via admin config for the account. Example API (admin-only):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/admin/accounts/ACMEX/config \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"inference": {"prefetch": {"enabled": false}}}'
```
Sam: I'll ask the customer if they want us to disable immediately while eng works on the metering change. Also asked billing for a provisional credit calculation.
billing-bot: Billing correlator found 18k tokens labeled `internal_prefetch` for acct=ACMEX between 2026-02-01 and 2026-02-28. Raw-metered: 1,180,412 tokens. User-facing served: 878,993 tokens. Delta: 301,419 tokens.
Ivy: thanks @billing-bot — that lines up. Sam, suggest offering a one-time credit for the warmup portion while ENG lands the exclusion flag. Also we should update the dashboard tooltip/FAQs to explain the difference.
Sam: Customer confirmed they'd like prefetch off for now and asked for a credit estimate + ETA for permanent fix. I've opened support ticket SUP-7621 and linked ENG-12345. ETA request: Alyssa, can engineering scope how long to implement metering_exclude flag + backfill recalculation?
Alyssa: rough estimate: 1 week to add tagging in runtime + metering pipeline and 2-3 days to run a backfill script for Feb delta once validated. If we prioritize, we can drop a patch in 3 business days for the tagging and 7 days for the pipeline change + backfill.
Kunal: good. Also consider adding an opt-out toggle per-route so customers who want aggressive prefetch can keep it but accept raw_metering.
Sam: noted. I'll (1) flip prefetch off for ACMEX, (2) send provisional credit numbers (billing), (3) set expectation with customer: eng ETA ~7 days for fix + backfill.
Ivy: tagging docs: we should add an entry in the billing FAQ about "why invoice tokens can exceed dashboard served tokens" and note internal prefetch/warmups and continuous batching. I'll draft the blurb after ENG confirms exact semantics.
Sam: done — prefetch disabled and customer notified. Will post updates here when billing posts credit and when ENG updates ENG-12345. :thumbsup:
